correctness.rationale: The nonnegative efficient core is exactly the edge-inequality polytope x_i+x_(i+1)>=1: matching lower bound proves sufficiency. Odd n=2m+1 has a unique core (0,1,...,0) because deleting any odd vertex leaves a perfect matching of worth m, forcing its payoff zero. For even n=2m≥4 disjoint base pairs force core first ratio 1 and x_(2j−1)=a_j, x_(2j)=1−a_j with 0≤a_1≤...≤a_m≤1. Defining m+1 nonnegative gaps g_0=a1, g_j=a_(j+1)−a_j, g_m=1−a_m summing 1, m+1 proper coalitions have worth m−1 and ratios 1+g_j/(m−1). Maximizing the second lexicographic level forces all gaps 1/(m+1), giving alpha2=1+1/(m²−1), unique even path allocation. All other nonfixed coalitions at this allocation have positive integer numerator surplus at least 1/(m+1) and worth ≤m−1. The exceptional n=2 has nonunique splits and is correctly excluded. Independently tested all proper positive-worth coalitions for P3 through P16 via induced matching DP and exact fractions; this is corroboration, not infinite proof.
residual_risks: All-order proof uses actual lexicographic fixed-face argument; finite rational grids alone could not prove it.
